newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Klaus urges Russia to rebuke envoy on NATO warning.
newsitem.headline: Klaus urges Russia to rebuke envoy on NATO warning.

text.p: Visiting Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Monday that Russia should make clear that its envoy to Prague did not speak officially when he cautioned the Czech Republic against NATO membership.
"We were shocked by the Russian ambassador's remarks... and I expect the Russian government to clearly dissociate itself from them," Klaus told a news conference during a one-day visit.
Nikolai Ryabov, Moscow's ambassador to Prague, said on Sunday that Russia could reconsider economic deals with Prague if the Czech Republic went ahead with its NATO membership bid.

Klaus said that even if the remarks were more than Ryabov's personal views the Czech Republic would still seek NATO entry. "But if this is indeed Russia's official view, then it is one more reason for us to join NATO as soon as possible," Klaus said.
During a joint news conference with his host, Klaus and Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn took sharply differing tacks on the issue of Romania's NATO membership bid.
"We are interested in Romania and Slovakia joining NATO, possibly in the first round," Horn said, reiterating Hungary's support for Romanian entry into NATO.
Klaus said only that "the Czech Republic will take into account Romania's bid for first-round NATO entry".
Last week, during Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's visit to Hungary, Horn voiced the firmest Hungarian support to date for Romania's NATO and European Union integration.

Prospective NATO membership and EU accession were the main themes during Klaus's one-day visit to Budapest, the first prime ministerial meeting between the two countries in four years. Klaus and Horn said their countries are not competing for NATO membership.
